title: PUT config endpoint stores AWS credentials in Vault and only sets credentialConfigured on the Mongo document
steps: Call PUT /api/cloud-posture-config/:projectId with a valid AWS credential payload
Inspect the resulting CloudPostureConfig Mongo document
Inspect Vault for the persisted secret
expectedResult: The Mongo document has providers.aws.credentialConfigured=true and no raw accessKeyId/secretAccessKey fields; the actual secret material exists only in Vault at the provider's configured path.

title: Test-connection with no credentials in the request body re-validates the already-stored configuration
description: When testProviderConnection is called without raw creds in the payload, config.controller.js sets isTestingStoredCreds=true, pulls the existing Vault-stored secret, and best-effort persists connectionHealth.status/lastTestedAt/message onto the config document.
steps: Ensure a project already has a verified AWS configuration
Call POST /api/cloud-posture-config/test-connection with only projectId and provider='aws' (no credentials in the body)
Inspect the CloudPostureConfig document afterward
expectedResult: The stored Vault credential is used for validation (not a fresh submission); connectionHealth.status, connectionHealth.lastTestedAt, and connectionHealth.message are updated to reflect the outcome of this re-test.

title: totalFindings on the dashboard includes PASS results while the sibling criticalFindings query filters to FAIL/ERROR only
description: Confirmed live defect (BUGS_FOUND.csv #17): the findingStats/totalFindings aggregation in dashboard.controller.js (getDashboardStats) has no status filter and counts PASS+FAIL+ERROR+SKIP+INFO together, while criticalFindingsByProvider in the same Promise.all correctly filters severity=CRITICAL AND status IN [FAIL,ERROR]. This produces an internally inconsistent dashboard.
preconditions: A completed scan exists with a known mix of PASS, FAIL, ERROR, and SKIP findings
steps: Call GET the dashboard stats endpoint for the project
Compare returned totalFindings against a manual count of FAIL+ERROR+CRITICAL findings only
Compare totalFindings against a manual count of all Finding docs regardless of status
expectedResult: Currently reproduces the bug: totalFindings equals the unfiltered all-status count, not a status-scoped count — flagged for remediation so the dashboard's 'Total Findings' label matches what it actually counts.

title: getCloudProviderResources accepts page/limit/search/service/severity but silently drops an unsupported 'status' filter param
description: Confirmed live defect (BUGS_FOUND.csv #20): resource.controller.js's getCloudProviderResources reads page, limit (default 500, capped 1000), search, service, and severity from the query string, but a 'status' param sent by the frontend has no corresponding server-side filter and is silently ignored.
steps: Call GET the provider dashboard/resources endpoint with ?status=FAIL&severity=HIGH
Compare the returned resource set against one fetched with only ?severity=HIGH
expectedResult: Currently reproduces the bug: both calls return the identical result set — the status parameter has no effect on filtering, even though the frontend UI exposes a status filter control.

title: Provider summary metric cards ignore the search/service/severity filters applied to the resource table below them
description: Confirmed live defect (BUGS_FOUND.csv #14): getProviderSummaryDetails (resource.controller.js) that feeds the provider page's metric cards is invoked with no filters at all, while the sibling resource-list query honors search/service/severity — so the cards always show unfiltered provider totals even when the visible table is filtered.
steps: Open a provider's dashboard endpoint response with a severity filter applied (e.g. ?severity=CRITICAL)
Compare the summary/metric-card counts in the response against the count of rows actually returned in the filtered resource list
expectedResult: Currently reproduces the bug: metric-card totals equal the full unfiltered provider totals and do not match the count of rows in the filtered resource list returned in the same response.

title: onCloudPostureScanCompleted derives dominantStatus with FAIL-over-PASS-over-SKIP priority and updates ClientControl.scores.cloud once per scan
preconditions: A scan's findings for a given checkId resolve to a UCL id present and active in ucl_master_v2
steps: Complete a scan where a given checkId has 3 FAIL and 2 PASS findings across resources; observe client-compliance-sync.service's onCloudPostureScanCompleted call
Complete a separate scan where the same checkId has 0 FAIL and 4 PASS findings
Complete a scan where the checkId's only findings are SKIP
Re-invoke the completion handler a second time for the same already-synced scan
expectedResult: Case 1 sets dominantStatus='FAIL' (fail>pass); case 2 sets 'PASS' (pass>0, no fail); case 3 sets 'SKIP'. The second invocation for the same scan is a no-op because scan.metadata.complianceSyncFired is already true — ClientControl.scores.cloud is not double-applied.

title: scan-scheduler.job's runDue() claims a due scheduled_recurring scan under a distributed lock and triggers exactly one scan
description: runDue() polls CloudPostureScan docs with status='scheduled_recurring' and schedule.nextRun<=now every 5s, using a Redis distributed lock, claims via findOneAndUpdate, and calls prowlerService.triggerScan. Verifies two scheduler instances (or two poll ticks racing) cannot double-fire the same due schedule.
preconditions: Two scheduler worker instances are running against the same Redis and MongoDB (simulating horizontal scaling)
steps: Set a schedule document's nextRun to a timestamp in the past
Allow both scheduler instances' 5-second poll ticks to run concurrently
expectedResult: Only one prowlerService.triggerScan call is made for that schedule; the losing instance's findOneAndUpdate claim attempt matches zero documents. metadata.runCount increments by exactly 1, not 2.

title: A stale active scan older than 30 minutes is auto-failed before a new scan is allowed to start on the same project
description: Before triggering a new scan, the backend sweeps for any active scan on the project with no state update in over 30 minutes and auto-fails it; a partial unique index prevents two concurrently-active scans existing for the same project.
preconditions: A scan for project P has status='running' with updatedAt older than 30 minutes (simulated stall)
steps: Attempt to trigger a new scan for project P
expectedResult: The stale scan is transitioned to 'failed' (with a reason indicating staleness) before the new scan is created; the new scan is created successfully and no duplicate-active-scan constraint violation occurs.
